name: Luna 24
short_status: Success: returned 170.1 g from Mare Crisium, 9 to 22 August 1976; the last Soviet lunar mission, and the last lunar samples anyone returned for 44 years.
tagline: Soviet Union · Sample return · 1976 · The space race Success

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 18 August 1976, Mare Crisium, at 12.7142 N, 62.2129 E (NSSDCA and the LROC 2016 coordinate update agree; LROC's superseded 2013 estimate of 12.7145 N still circulates)

facts.label: The accidental sampling site
facts.value: Landed on the northwest rim of a 64 m crater, ~2.3 km from Luna 23, and sampled its excavated ejecta rather than typical mare surface

facts.label: Sample
facts.value: 170.1 grams collected by sample arm and drill and sealed in the return capsule

facts.label: Analyzed depths
facts.value: Laboratory studies used core material from depths of 118, 143 and 184 cm

facts.label: Ascent and return
facts.value: Capsule launched from the Moon 19 August 1976 at 05:25 UT; landed 22 August at 05:55 UT about 200 km southeast of Surgut, western Siberia

facts.label: Water report
facts.value: February 1978: Akhmanova, Dement'ev and Markov (Vernadsky Institute) report ~0.1% water by mass in the samples via 3-micron infrared absorption, in Geokhimiya

facts.label: Luna 23 prequel
facts.value: Luna 23 (November 1974) hit the surface too fast and fell on its side; LROC images published 16 March 2012 show the toppled lander 2.3 km from Luna 24

facts.label: The long gap
facts.value: Next lunar sample return: China's Chang'e 5, which landed its capsule 16 December 2020, 44 years later

facts.label: The Russian sequel
facts.value: Russia's next lunar landing attempt, Luna 25, crashed on 19 August 2023; NASA's LRO imaged its fresh crater

timeline: Soft-lands in Mare Crisium, 2.3 km from the toppled Luna 23; drill collects 170.1 g of core
05:25 UT: ascent stage launches the sample capsule off the Moon
05:55 UT: capsule lands ~200 km SE of Surgut, western Siberia: the last Soviet lunar mission is complete
Vernadsky Institute team reports ~0.1% water by mass in the Luna 24 core (Geokhimiya), largely unnoticed in the West
LROC images solve the 35-year sample mismatch: Luna 24 sat on the rim of a 64 m crater and sampled its deep-dug ejecta
Chang'e 3 makes the first lunar soft landing since Luna 24, 37 years later
Chang'e 5 returns the first lunar samples since Luna 24, 44 years later
Russia's Luna 25, the first Luna since 1976, crashes; LRO images the impact crater
